page_title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate

summary.name: Multiagent Debate (arXiv 2305.14325)
summary.one_liner: A 2023 arXiv research paper proposing that multiple language model instances propose and debate their answers over several rounds to reach a common final answer, improving reasoning and factuality.
use_cases: improve answer accuracy from language models
math word problem solving with llms
summary.what_it_does: ["Runs multiple instances of a language model that each propose an answer and reasoning process.", "Lets the instances read each other's responses and debate over multiple rounds.", "Converges on a common final answer after the debate rounds.", "Reports improved mathematical and strategic reasoning and better factual validity with fewer hallucinations, per the abstract.", "Applies to existing black-box models using the same procedure and prompts across all tasks studied."]
notable: Works with black-box models without needing access to internals
Uses identical procedure and prompts across all evaluated tasks
Listed in the e2b-dev awesome-ai-agents collection
caveats: Page is only the arXiv abstract listing; full results and limitations are in the PDF, which was not reviewed
Multiple model instances per query implies higher compute and cost than a single call
